scenes.text: In our made-up subscription-billing system, an agent works the nightly reconcile. Whose name? Its own identity: billing ops agent. Not a shared login, not a person's. So the log says who. [pause] Its job, written down: compare our ledger with the payment processor's report, work out why they differ, tell a person. And one named owner, who answers for it.

data.label: A MADE-UP EXAMPLE  ·  THE AGENT THAT WORKS THE NIGHTLY RECONCILE

data.caption: Its own identity. Its job, written down. One named owner.

scenes.text: What may it touch? The least the job needs. It reads the ledger, and the processor's report. It writes in one place: a case, for a person. [pause] It can't change the ledger, move money, or change its own access. [pause] That's enforced by the system, not by the prompt. An instruction can be talked around. A permission that isn't there can't be.

scenes.text: Some things are out of reach. The card number: the processor holds it, and we hold a token. The processor's key: a tool fetches the report, with a read-only key the agent is never shown. Customer details: only the fields the job needs. No name, no email.

scenes.text: One made-up night. Two forty A.M. The processor's report: nine hundred eighty-nine charges. Our ledger: nine hundred eighty-eight. The agent reads both, and finds the one: a thirty-dollar renewal, charged by the processor. Our side timed out, the retries ran out, and it never reached the ledger.

scenes.text: A near miss, also made up. At setup, this agent's access was copied from a support role. So it could issue refunds, and never said so. Then its owner reviewed every permission: needed? Used? Three stay. Refunds: not needed, never used. Removed. [pause] Agents read text they didn't write, like a note on a payment, and text can be written to steer them. With the spare permission, a refund could go out. Without it, the system says no.

scenes.text: Two more, for a bad day. A limit: say, twenty cases a night. Past that, it stops, and tells a person. A stop switch: its owner turns off this one identity, and only this agent stops.

scenes.text: So, to recap. One agent, one job, one identity. The least access, enforced by the system. Every action logged, where the agent can't change it. A person decides on money, and on the ledger.

scenes.text: Which gives us rule nine, for your agents. Use only your own identity, and only the access the job needs. Never borrow a login, or work around a no. Give your reason with every action. Don't move money, or change the ledger, unless a person has released it. Otherwise: prepare it, and hand it over. If you can do more than the job needs, say so.
